title: The Mafia may be keeping fentanyl out of Italy
summary: This Economist article explores the unexpected phenomenon of Italian organized crime preventing fentanyl from entering Italy, apparently viewing the deadly synthetic opioid as bad for business and harmful to their 'customers'. Unlike the devastating fentanyl crises in the US and other countries, Italy has largely avoided this epidemic, with the Mafia allegedly acting as a de facto barrier.
problem_solved: Explains why Italy has largely avoided the fentanyl crisis that has devastated other Western countries.
why_valuable: Offers a counterintuitive perspective on organized crime's role in public health outcomes and illustrates how even criminal enterprises have rational economic incentives.
